stem: Carbamazepine is used to control certain types of which neurologic events?

options.label: A
options.misconception: None — carbamazepine controls certain types of seizures.
options.explanation: MedlinePlus lists carbamazepine to control certain types of seizures, and also to treat trigeminal neuralgia and manic or mixed episodes.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Assumes any sudden, transient neurologic deficit is a seizure.
options.explanation: Transient ischemic attacks are brief focal deficits from cerebral ischemia; prevention uses antiplatelet therapy and risk-factor control, not antiseizure drugs.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Mistakes a brief faint, which may include a few jerks, for an epileptic seizure.
options.explanation: Vasovagal syncope is transient loss of consciousness from reflex hypotension and bradycardia; it is not epileptic and needs no antiseizure drug.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Assumes antiseizure drugs treat every paroxysmal disorder of consciousness.
options.explanation: Narcoleptic sleep attacks come from loss of hypocretin (orexin) neurons and are treated with wake-promoting drugs such as modafinil, not carbamazepine.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Assumes a neurologic crisis of any kind responds to an antiseizure drug.
options.explanation: Myasthenic crisis is autoimmune neuromuscular respiratory failure treated with IVIG or plasma exchange; carbamazepine has no role.

context: Learning objective: Carbamazepine controls certain types of seizures and also treats trigeminal neuralgia and manic or mixed episodes.
